questions.stem: The lamp in this circuit will light.
questions.image_alt: A circuit with a cell, a lamp and a closed switch.
questions.explanation: The loop is complete and the switch is closed, so electricity flows round and the lamp lights.

questions.stem: Why is the lamp off in this circuit?
questions.image_alt: A circuit with a cell, a lamp and an open switch.
questions.explanation: The open switch makes a gap in the loop. Electricity cannot flow round, so the lamp stays off.

questions.stem: Match each part of a circuit to its job.
questions.explanation: A cell pushes electricity round. A wire carries it. A switch turns the circuit on and off. A lamp gives light.

questions.stem: Is it safe or not safe? Sort the actions.
items: asking an adult to plug in
touching a switch with wet hands
questions.explanation: We use torches with batteries and ask an adult to plug things in. We never touch switches with wet hands or poke sockets.

questions.stem: Does it use electricity? Sort the pictures.
questions.explanation: A fan, a television and a mobile phone use electricity. A ball, a chair and a teddy bear do not.

questions.stem: A circuit is a loop.
questions.explanation: A circuit is a complete loop. Electricity flows round it from the cell, through the lamp and back.

questions.stem: Electricity from the wall is safe to touch.
questions.explanation: Electricity from the wall is dangerous. Never touch sockets or wires.

questions.stem: A switch can make a gap in a circuit.
questions.explanation: Opening a switch makes a gap, so the circuit is off. Closing it fills the gap.

questions.stem: A lamp lights when the circuit is ___.
questions.explanation: Electricity can only flow round a complete circuit with no gaps.

questions.stem: A cell is a battery that stores ___.
questions.explanation: A cell stores electricity and pushes it round the circuit.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to make a lamp light.
sequence: Join the cell, wires and lamp in a loop.
questions.explanation: Join the parts in a loop, check there are no gaps, close the switch and then the lamp lights.

questions.stem: Which part turns a circuit on and off?
questions.explanation: A switch opens and closes the circuit. A lamp gives light and a wire carries electricity.

questions.stem: Which picture shows where solar electricity comes from?
questions.explanation: A solar panel turns sunlight into electricity.

questions.stem: Where does electricity come from? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Sunlight, wind and moving water can all make electricity. A stone and a teddy bear cannot.

questions.stem: There are no wires on Shuvo's char. Where does his electricity come from?
questions.explanation: Shuvo's family has a solar panel on the roof. It turns sunlight into electricity.

questions.stem: Anika's hands are wet. A switch is on the wall. What should she do?
questions.explanation: Wet hands and electricity are dangerous. Anika asks an adult for help.

questions.stem: Mina's toy light does not work. A wire has fallen off the cell. Why?
questions.explanation: The wire is part of the loop. With a wire off, there is a gap and electricity cannot flow.

questions.stem: At night, Shuvo's battery lights the lamps.
questions.explanation: The solar panel charges the battery in the day. At night the battery lights the lamps.

questions.stem: Why is a solar panel useful on the char?
questions.model_answer: There are no electricity wires on the char, so the solar panel makes electricity from sunlight.
questions.explanation: There are no electricity wires on the char. A solar panel makes electricity from sunlight.

questions.stem: What happens to the bulb in a complete loop?

sim.task: Open Circuit Construction Kit: DC. Drag a battery, a light bulb and wires onto the board. Join them in one complete loop with no gaps. Watch the bulb.

questions.explanation: A bulb lights only when the loop is complete. Electricity flows from the battery through the bulb and back.

questions.stem: The bulb stays lit when the switch is open.

sim.task: Open Circuit Construction Kit: DC. Make a loop with a battery, a bulb and wires, and add a switch. Click the switch to open it, then click it again to close it. Watch the bulb each time.

questions.explanation: An open switch makes a gap in the loop, so the bulb goes out. Closing the switch lights it again.

questions.stem: A wire is off the loop. You close the switch. Does the lamp light?

options.text: No, it still has a gap.

questions.explanation: The missing wire leaves a gap, so closing the switch does not help.

questions.stem: Each torch uses 2 cells. How many cells do 3 torches need?
questions.explanation: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6, so 3 torches need 6 cells.

questions.stem: Metal things such as a coin let electricity pass through.
questions.explanation: Metals let electricity through. Things like a rubber eraser do not.
